title: Reachability: an operator doctor for five organs, and four kept deliberately unreachable
head: 564de83c0099dbabd53e20fa2e18c93138b78004
body:
Completes the **MAKE REACHABLE** step the swarm construction law requires, for the nine organs merged in #469–#478. Based on `b71265304c01b546dc8896dd7d8bf0159f581591` (the spine head after those merges).

The reachability ratchet caught the nine new modules with no entry point and no classification. They needed two different answers, because they are not alike.

## Five get a real entry point

`scripts/sovereign-organs-doctor.mjs` exercises one load-bearing refusal per organ and exits non-zero when a boundary is gone:

| organ | boundary checked |
|---|---|
| forecast-parent-organ | 20 cases from 1 source → `REFERENCE_CLASS_UNDERPOWERED`, `baseRate` null |
| forecast-decision-boundary | EV 9,999,999 with ruin → `NOT_RECOMMENDABLE__IRREVERSIBLE_RUIN` |
| forecast-adversarial-ensemble | 10 forecasters / 1 ancestor → 1 effective vote |
| genesis-mechanism-compiler | claimed `VERIFIED_FACT` from `VENDOR_MATERIAL` → `VENDOR_CLAIM` |
| genesis-boundary-experiment | exhausted search, no mechanism → `UNKNOWN` |

It asserts behaviour rather than importing modules to prove they parse — a doctor that only imported would report health it never measured. Proven non-vacuous: with the ruin firewall deleted it returns `BOUNDARY_LOST` and exits 1.

## Four are kept unreachable, on purpose

The Personal Civilization organs are classified `DELIBERATELY_UNREACHABLE`. They compose `personal-civilization-core`, which already carries that category for a reason worth quoting:

> Holds the founder's private life state — the one data class that is not the company's. Every entry point in this repository is autonomous: the scheduler, the worker and the mesh tick all run without a person present. A path from any of them to this module would mean private life records could be read, derived from, or exported by a lane acting on its own.

Reachability is inherited, so a script reaching these organs is a path from an autonomous lane to that store.

**An earlier draft of this doctor imported them**, to check their refusals too. The ratchet failed with:

```
these modules are unreachable on purpose and something now reaches them:
  src/personal-civilization-core.mjs
Remove the entry point. Do not reclassify the module to make this pass.
```

That instruction is right, and I followed it in the direction it points: the entry point was removed, not the classification softened. Checking that a boundary holds is not worth opening it. The doctor now reports those four under `privateOrgansDeliberatelyNotChecked`, so their absence is a stated decision rather than an oversight someone later "fixes".

Their `gate` key is **absent** rather than null, per the ratchet's rule that a gate would name a condition under which wiring becomes correct — and for this category there is none.

```

  -> ALL_BOUNDARIES_HELD, checked 5, held 5, broken 0, exit 0

with the ruin firewall removed
  -> BOUNDARY_LOST, held 7 broken 2, exit 1        (non-vacuity check)

  -> # tests 18   # pass 18   # fail 0

live reachability: 429 src modules | 177 production | 116 operator-only | 136 no entry point
```

## Boundaries

The doctor performs no I/O, contacts nothing, and carries `businessEffectAuthority: 'NONE'`. Its own note states what it does not prove: that any forecast is accurate, any candidate is good, or that the full suite passes. No private life data appears in it — the one check that needed a private record was removed along with the import.

title: PCE-04, PCE-06, PCE-07: possibility portfolio, capability skeleton, and the smallest honest experiment
head: c013a63699c94970b9423e7dc191fc2a93890252
body:
Night-swarm child for issue #463. Packets **PCE-04**, **PCE-06**, **PCE-07** as one organ.

Base: `047e36c6eb0a27c3deabbba581c05e29ab597f3d` (exact PR #458 head).

## Write surfaces

- `src/personal-civilization-possibility.mjs` (363 lines)
- `tests/personal-civilization-possibility.test.mjs` (299 lines)

Exactly two new files.

## What it does

**PCE-04 — possibility portfolio.** Materially distinct families (`NON_OBVIOUS`, `STATUS_QUO`, `REVERSIBLE_TRIAL`, `STAGED_COMMITMENT`, `EXIT`, `CAPABILITY_FIRST`, `ENVIRONMENT_FIRST`), deduplicated by causal shape so cosmetic rewordings collapse while genuinely different paths survive. Each possibility records what must be true for it to be reachable, what it opens, and what it closes.

The load-bearing rule: **optionality is not automatically maximised**. A deliberate commitment that closes branches for depth, mastery, love or loyalty must not be scored as strictly worse than a path that keeps everything open. The mutation for this injected `optionality = 1 - closes.length * 0.2` — a change that looks perfectly reasonable and quietly converts commitment into a penalty — and a test catches it.

**No scalar score for a life exists anywhere in the module.** Verified by grep: no `totalScore`, `overallScore`, `lifeScore` or `combinedScore` field.

**PCE-06 — Osteogenesis.** Almost entirely composition rather than new logic, which is the honest outcome here: `src/human-capability-genome.mjs` already contained `growSkeleton` and `findBottleneck`, fully satisfying "minimum skeleton" and "binding constraint", and it already carries the character-defect guard (`DURABLE_LIMIT` requires strong evidence). The genuinely missing piece was high-transfer ranking by `unlocks` edges — preferring capabilities that open many futures over brittle optimisation for one. The rest is a thin wrapper.

**PCE-07 — experience plan.** Compiles a possibility into the smallest authentic reversible experience that would reveal whether it actually suits the person, recording reversibility, cost, time, what it would reveal and what would falsify the possibility.

`SPEND`, `TRAVEL_COMMITMENT` and `THIRD_PARTY_INVOLVEMENT` are gated behind a distinct `LIFE_EXPERIENCE_COMMITMENT` founder-authority grant — deliberately **not** reusing the core's `PRIVATE_LIFE_STATE` grant, since permission to hold private life data is a different authority domain from permission to spend money or involve another person. Conflating them would let one consent silently widen into the other.

Rest and joy are accepted with **no productivity field in the schema at all**, so they cannot be asked to justify themselves.

title: PCE-02, PCE-03: living model and graph provenance — a person is not a fixed label
head: 4a9573bbb2adf6f98f0d42745e134d4818bd72ab
body:
Night-swarm child for issue #463. Packets **PCE-02** and **PCE-03** as one organ.

Base: `047e36c6eb0a27c3deabbba581c05e29ab597f3d` (exact PR #458 head).

## Write surfaces

- `src/personal-civilization-model-graph.mjs`
- `tests/personal-civilization-model-graph.test.mjs`

Exactly two new files (`git diff --name-only 047e36c6..HEAD` verified).

## What it does

**PCE-02 — the model is a person over time, not a label.** `deriveLivingModel` already derives a model from records, but it stores flat, untyped, non-competing claims with no supersession concept. This adds:

- **Typed hypotheses**, one of ten: `TRAIT`, `TEMPORARY_STATE`, `SKILL_DEFICIT`, `HABIT`, `ENVIRONMENT_EFFECT`, `PREFERENCE`, `VALUE`, `SELF_STORY`, `INSUFFICIENT_EXPOSURE`, `UNKNOWN`.
- **Competing hypotheses held side by side**, never collapsed into a single conclusion.
- **A forbidden-promotion table.** `SKILL_DEFICIT`, `ENVIRONMENT_EFFECT`, `TEMPORARY_STATE` and `INSUFFICIENT_EXPOSURE` cannot be promoted to `TRAIT`. This is the "I am bad at X" failure, where evidence that supports *"I am inexperienced at X"* or *"my current environment makes X hard"* silently hardens into a permanent identity claim.
- **Supersession preserves the prior.** A superseded hypothesis survives with its supersession reason; a model of a person is not allowed to become an identity prison by deleting what it used to think.
- **Evidence-weighted ranking**, so an unevidenced hypothesis never outranks an evidenced one.

**PCE-03 — provenance that survives.** `life-knowledge-graph.mjs` has edges, basis, contradictions and `authenticate`, but no binding to the private-record layer at all. This adds:

- Every edge asserted through `assertProvenancedEdge` requires an existing private-record source and carries origin, time, basis and privacy class.
- **`assertionKind` is computed strictly from `basis`, never accepted from caller input**, so an inference cannot present itself as an observation.
- `reconcileGraphAfterDeletion` reuses the core's own `derivedClosure` rather than a shallow existence check, so a claim citing a record that is only *transitively* derived from a deleted root is pruned too — matching exactly what `deletePrivateRecords` would remove. Otherwise a derived graph claim outlives the deletion of the thing it came from, and deletion becomes cosmetic.

## Honest limitation

The TRAIT-promotion guard is **structural, not semantic**: it blocks the type transition outright but cannot read the statement text and judge whether a particular promotion is genuinely justified. That is the right boundary for a deterministic module with no NLP, but it means a caller who mislabels a claim's type at registration time is a separate problem this does not solve.

## Evidence actually executed at this head

```
node --check src/personal-civilization-model-graph.mjs    -> OK
node --test  tests/personal-civilization-model-graph.test.mjs
  # tests 18   # pass 18   # fail 0

node --test tests/personal-civilization-core.test.mjs      (regression, file untouched)
  # tests 22   # pass 22   # fail 0
```

Guard-deletion mutations, file restored and diffed identical after each:

| mutation | tests killed |
|---|---|
| forbidden TRAIT-promotion table removed | 2 |
| evidence-strength ranking sort removed | 1 |
| superseded hypothesis dropped instead of preserved | 2 |
| `assertionKind` hardcoded to `OBSERVATION` | 1 |
| deletion-closure pruning removed | 2 |
| hypothesis-type validity check removed | 1 |

**A finding from the mutation run worth surfacing.** The first attempt at the ranking mutation *did not* fail its test — the evidenced hypothesis happened to be registered first, so insertion order coincided with the correct answer and the assertion passed with the sort deleted. The fixture was rewritten to register the unevidenced hypothesis first, and the guard is now genuinely load-bearing. I re-ran that mutation independently to confirm: deleting the sort kills exactly one test.

That is the failure mode mutation testing exists to catch — a test that passes for the wrong reason looks identical to a test that works.

## Reuse

Imported, not reimplemented: `founderAuthorized`, `deriveLivingModel`, `derivedClosure` from `personal-civilization-core.mjs`; `edge` with its `EDGE_KINDS` / `EDGE_BASIS` validation from `life-knowledge-graph.mjs`. Neither packet was already closed — verified by reading both modules in full.

title: PCE-05, PCE-08: decision packet and the loop back to reality
head: e8fde11e1dca849b58bb0d302dd5748903a61bf6
body:
Night-swarm child for issue #463. Packets **PCE-05** and **PCE-08** as one organ.

Base: `047e36c6eb0a27c3deabbba581c05e29ab597f3d` (exact PR #458 head).

## Write surfaces

- `src/personal-civilization-decision-loop.mjs` (444 lines)
- `tests/personal-civilization-decision-loop.test.mjs` (303 lines)

Two new files. Verified: `git diff --name-only 047e36c6..HEAD` returns exactly these two.

## What it does

**PCE-05 — decision packet.** Binds the decision statement, the materially distinct options (never narrowed to the winner — every option keeps its own outcome-distribution slot), forecast strength, key assumptions, what could make it wrong, irreversible consequences, unknown unknowns, the highest-value next experiment, update conditions, and the mandatory `FOUNDER_REMAINS_CHOOSER` line.

The value-boundary refusal is **derived from `compareLifeOptions`'s own domination/tradeoff output** rather than reimplemented, so it inherits that module's no-total guarantee instead of growing a second opinion about when options are incomparable. When a genuine tradeoff has no dominating option, the packet returns `NO_RECOMMENDATION__VALUE_BOUNDARY_REACHED` and picks no winner.

Regret and option value are attached through a separate `attachRegretAndOptionValue` call rather than folded into packet construction — regret inputs are per-option, and forcing a caller to fabricate them just to obtain a packet would manufacture exactly the false precision the packet exists to avoid.

**PCE-08 — the loop back to reality.** `recordPacketOutcomeForecast` and `closePacketLoop` compose `recordForecast` / `scoreForecast` / `decisionQuality` verbatim, so outcome and decision quality stay demonstrably separate: a lucky bad decision does not become doctrine, and an unlucky good one is not mislearned as a mistake.

`derivePacketAsPrivateRecord`, `exportOrDeleteDecisionHistory` and `decisionClosure` compose `deriveLivingModel` / `exportPrivateState` / `deletePrivateRecords` / `derivedClosure`. A decision summary is only ever stored **with explicit `derivedFrom` provenance**, which is what makes it reachable by the private core's deletion closure. Without that, a derived summary would quietly outlive the deletion of the record it came from — memory sovereignty defeated by a cache.

## Reuse: this module wrote no new hashing, sealing, scoring or deletion logic

Composed verbatim: the whole forecast ledger from `reality-calibration-ledger.mjs`; the whole private store from `personal-civilization-core.mjs`; `forecast-stack.mjs` (`valueOfInformation`, `regretGeometry`, `decisionShelfLife`, `predictionHalfLife`, `adversarialFutureSelves`, `strengthProfile`, `buildForecast`); and `life-decision-dimensions.mjs` (`scoreOption`, `compareLifeOptions`, `goodhartRisk`).

title: FORECAST-08: adversarial ensemble — agreement is not evidence when the sources share an ancestor
head: 1686f73241acdec96803ed9928addd469d71a6fd
body:
Night-swarm child for issue #463. Packet **FORECAST-08**.

Base: `047e36c6eb0a27c3deabbba581c05e29ab597f3d` (exact PR #458 head at claim time).

## Write surfaces

- `src/forecast-adversarial-ensemble.mjs`
- `tests/forecast-adversarial-ensemble.test.mjs`

Two new files, nothing else.

## The one idea

Ten forecasters agreeing is either strong evidence or one opinion repeated ten times, and nothing in the agreement itself tells you which. This module makes that difference computable.

**Evidence ancestry is required** on every submission. A forecaster that will not say where its evidence came from cannot be checked for correlation, and an uncheckable submission silently becomes a free extra vote for whatever it already believed.

**Clustering by shared ancestry.** Forecasters linked by any shared source — transitively — form one cluster worth **one effective vote**, plus a small credit (0.25) for members holding evidence nobody else in the cluster holds. Partial independence stays partial: reading one extra source does not restore full independence to a clone. The raw count is reported beside the effective count so the gap stays visible rather than being quietly resolved toward the larger, more flattering number.

**Only discounted agreement reaches the strength profile.** Agreement among copies is not evidence and must not be able to raise a strength score.

**Adversarial testing is not optional to report.** An ensemble with no attacks recorded is labelled `ENSEMBLE_ADVERSARIALLY_UNTESTED`; it does not inherit confidence from a consensus it was never asked to defend. A vague objection is not an attack — attacks must be typed, or they degrade into recorded disagreement.

**Model ecology drops nothing.** Discarding outliers looks like noise reduction and is sometimes the removal of the only forecaster that was right. Dissenting and heterodox models are preserved and named. A minority model does not win by being different and is not erased for being outnumbered.

**Bias flags are raised, never resolved.** A review that clears a conclusion is doing the opposite of its job.

## The test that carries the argument

The central test runs the **same ten forecasters, agreeing on the same outcome by the same margin**, and changes only whether their evidence traces to one ancestor or to ten:

| | correlated | independent |
|---|---|---|
| raw agreement rate | identical | identical |
| effective independent count | **1** | **10** |
| consensus class | `CORRELATED_AGREEMENT` | `INDEPENDENT_CONVERGENCE` |
| evidential agreement | strictly lower | strictly higher |

If those two ever produce the same finding, the module has stopped doing the only thing it is for — and the test asserts exactly that.

title: PCE-01: private capture — a thought enters the loop without becoming a goal

Night-swarm child for issue #463. Packet **PCE-01**.

Base: `047e36c6eb0a27c3deabbba581c05e29ab597f3d` (exact PR #458 head at claim time).

## Write surfaces

Two new files, 914 insertions. `personal-civilization-core.mjs` is **composed, not modified**.

## Was PCE-01 already closed? Partly — and the gap was specific

The brief for this packet required reporting honestly if the core already covered it. It covered the *holding* end and not the *capture* end.

`personal-civilization-core.mjs` had no notion of a Will Event and no consent or opacity flags at all. The decisive gap: `normalizePrivateRecord` keeps the fields it knows and drops the rest, so a `do-not-model` flag passed as an ordinary record field **would have vanished during normalization, and the record would then have been modelled anyway — silently, while looking correct**. That is the failure this layer exists to prevent, and it is why the answer was a new composing layer rather than either a duplicate or a "nothing to do here".

## What it does

**Will Event capture.** A raw thought, desire, curiosity, intuition, aversion, uncertainty, fear, contradiction, veto, commitment or revision — including "I do not know what I want", which is accepted as a valid capture rather than rejected as malformed. A captured Will Event does **not** become a goal, task or commitment without an explicit separate `promoteCapture` step. Promotion does not auto-copy the source thought.

**Consent and opacity at capture time.** `do-not-model`, `do-not-infer-from`, `do-not-persist`, `do-not-predict-from`, and a right-not-to-know marker for findings the founder asked not to receive (`partitionFindingsForFounder`). A `do-not-model` record is excluded from the derived living model by **withholding it from the core before derivation**, so exclusion is structural rather than a filter the core could be talked out of.

**Privacy routing.** `captureDestinationAllowed` calls the core's `privateDestinationAllowed` rather than re-deciding it, so weakening the core surfaces in these tests too. `PRIVATE_LIFE_DATA` to a public or networked destination is refused.

**Non-totalization.** A record the founder declines to classify or explain is still accepted. Capture never requires justification to accept a thought.

The first draft had the consent check in two places. The mutation run showed the store-filter layer had **no behaviour the claim-level precheck did not already mask** — an untestable "safety" layer, which is worse than none, because it invites belief in a protection no test pins. **GENESIS-06 — ontology escalation.** The full seven-stage loop, `NO_ESCALATION_REQUIRED` when nothing distorts, and rejection when a proposed concept makes no prediction or admits no counterexample — the gate that separates Ontogenesis from inventing vocabulary. title: FORECAST-05..07: decision boundary, ruin firewall, and the right to refuse
head: 8639811e6ee83d2071b3c424599b68a16bcc9b9e
body:
Night-swarm child for issue #463. Packets **FORECAST-05, 06, 07** closed as one organ.

Base: `047e36c6eb0a27c3deabbba581c05e29ab597f3d` (exact PR #458 head at claim time).

## Write surfaces

- `src/forecast-decision-boundary.mjs`
- `tests/forecast-decision-boundary.test.mjs`

Two new files, nothing else — no `package.json` edit, since `scripts/run-tests.mjs` discovers `tests/*.test.mjs` by directory scan.

## What it does

**FORECAST-05 — flip thresholds.** Answers canon's required question: what evidence would change the recommendation. An assumption only counts toward a flip threshold if someone named the specific observation that would overturn it. *"This depends on the market holding"* is a caveat; *"this reverses if two consecutive quarters contract"* is a trigger, and only the second can ever fire. A recommendation where nothing was named is returned **fragile** rather than refused — refusing it would simply teach callers to invent a trigger.

**FORECAST-06 — ruin-aware regret.** Composes `regretGeometry` and `valueOfInformation` from `forecast-stack.mjs` rather than recomputing them, and adds the ruin firewall:

- An irreversible option that never answers the ruin question is **refused**. Silence is how a catastrophic branch gets carried forward as though it had been considered.
- Ruin declared on an option also marked reversible is contradictory input, not caution — the meaning of ruin is that recovery is unavailable.
- An option carrying ruin is **not recommendable at any expected value**. The expected value stays in the record and loses anyway, so what was traded is visible rather than hidden.
- No combined score, ever. The tail is never averaged into the mean.

**FORECAST-07 — uncertainty class and the refusal boundary.** All five canonical terminal states are reachable, as exact strings rather than paraphrases, because the entire value of a refusal is that a caller can match on it — a refusal phrased freshly each time is prose, and prose gets summarised into a recommendation downstream.

Knight's classes change the **selection rule**, not just a label: `RISK` selects by expected value, `UNCERTAINTY` by lowest cost of being wrong, `DEEP_UNCERTAINTY` by reversibility and option value, `IGNORANCE` by reversible probes only. A missing answer never upgrades the class — not knowing whether the state space is known is itself evidence that it is not.

Incomparability is Pareto-tested. When each option wins on a value the other loses, no ordering exists that does not first decide which value matters more, and that decision is not the system's to make: it returns `NO_RECOMMENDATION__VALUE_BOUNDARY_REACHED` and picks no winner. Options with no declared values are *undescribed*, not incomparable — a refusal that costs nothing means nothing.

**Order of operations carries the argument.** Termination runs first, because a decision you cannot reason about should not receive a robustness table. Ruin is removed before anything is compared, so a catastrophic option never gets the chance to win on average. Incomparability is tested only among survivors, so a ruinous option cannot manufacture a value boundary. Selection happens last and is the least interesting step.

Base: `047e36c6eb0a27c3deabbba581c05e29ab597f3d` (exact PR #458 head at claim time).

## Write surfaces

Two new files. Nothing else touched — no `package.json` edit, because `scripts/run-tests.mjs` discovers `tests/*.test.mjs` by directory scan, so this suite joins `test:deterministic` without a shared-file edit that would conflict with sibling children.

- `src/forecast-parent-organ.mjs`
- `tests/forecast-parent-organ.test.mjs`

## What it does

**FORECAST-01 — reference class / base rate.** Independence is counted over *sources*, not rows. The failure mode is not too few cases; it is twenty cases that all trace back to one analyst report, which looks like a large sample right until it is wrong in the same direction at once. A correlated or underpowered class still shows its raw fraction — hiding the arithmetic would be its own dishonesty — but is refused the name "base rate". Survivorship, selection, publication and availability biases are each either corrected or named as uncorrected.

**FORECAST-02 — scenario distribution.** A band, never a point estimate. An inherently unmeasurable outcome ("did this life feel worthwhile") returns null percentiles and keeps its narrative cases, because attaching a P50 there is invention rather than caution. A probability quoted past two decimals is *refused rather than rounded*, so that offering false precision cannot pass silently.

**FORECAST-03 — hindcast / backtest.** A method carries trusted weight only after being scored against outcomes already known. Trials with no known outcome are refused as a scoring basis, since counting them lets a method accumulate a record without ever having been checked.

**FORECAST-04 — calibration update triggers.** See the dedupe note below; the genuinely new part is `forecastUpdateTriggers`.

**The parent** composes all four and is allowed to return `FORECAST_UNKNOWN`. That is the justification for the organ: a compiler that always emitted a range would be a slower route to manufactured precision, and the slowness would make it more convincing rather than less.

## Dedupe: the ledger delegates, it does not compete

`src/reality-calibration-ledger.mjs` already exists and already seals forecasts with a SHA-256 content hash. An earlier draft of this module grew its own parallel ledger with a boolean `scored` flag. That was removed before commit — the existing ledger's own comment names exactly why a flag is weaker ("a flag can be set to false by the same code that wants to edit").

Resolution:
- `recordForecast`, `scoreForecast` and `calibrationSummary` are **re-exported** from this module, so a caller composing a full forecast reaches the existing sealed ledger instead of writing a third softer copy.
- Only the genuinely different *shape* lives here: the existing ledger takes categorical outcomes whose probabilities sum to one, while this organ forecasts a continuous P10/P50/P90 band, which does not fit that shape without distorting it.
- The banded entry is sealed with the **same content-hash construction**, so the repository has one tamper mechanism, not two.

`forecastUpdateTriggers` is the part neither module had. Scoring is retrospective by construction — it can only speak once an outcome exists — which leaves the gap where the quiet failure lives: a forecast whose assumptions stopped holding months ago, still being acted on, still unscored because the question has not resolved. It reads the triggers the forecaster committed to at record time and reports which fired. Only assumptions *actually recorded at forecast time* can be falsified, so an inconvenient fact cannot be relabelled a trigger to justify a rewrite. It returns a verdict and never edits.

## Evidence actually executed at this head

```
node --check src/forecast-parent-organ.mjs                 -> clean
node --check tests/forecast-parent-organ.test.mjs          -> clean
node --test  tests/forecast-parent-organ.test.mjs
  # tests 43   # pass 43   # fail 0   # cancelled 0   # skipped 0
```

Mutation pressure — each guard deleted in turn, baseline restored after each:

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| source-independence guard forced false | 42 pass / **1 fail** |
| seal verification bypassed | 42 pass / **1 fail** |
| post-outcome revision freeze bypassed | 42 pass / **1 fail** |
| `UNKNOWN` collapse forced to always-widen | 41 pass / **2 fail** |
| recorded-assumption check bypassed | 42 pass / **1 fail** |
| restored baseline | **43 pass / 0 fail** |

Every guard is load-bearing: deleting it fails a test that names that specific failure. No test was weakened to obtain green.

## Boundaries

- Every returned result, success and refusal alike, carries `businessEffectAuthority: 'NONE'`.
- Reasoning ends at `RECOMMENDATION`; the compiled forecast carries `PREDICTION_NEVER_CREATES_AUTHORITY__THE_CHOOSER_REMAINS_THE_CHOOSER`.
- No customer, cleared-payment, acceptance, retention, provider-callability or forecast-accuracy truth is asserted. Passing tests prove the refusals hold, not that any forecast is correct about the world.
- Reachability: exported ESM composed by `forecast-stack.mjs` and `reality-calibration-ledger.mjs`; no scheduler, network, provider or credential surface is touched.
- No private life data appears in source, tests or fixtures.

Continues into the 215 unbuilt rows left after #455, and answers the question I flagged there rather than leaving it open.

## The flagged question, resolved

`truthPriority` is an **ordered evidence ranking**, not six unenforced laws. `HYPOTHESIS` and `DRAFT_BRANCH_EVIDENCE` are rungs, and asking which module enforces a rung is a category error. Its sibling `truthClasses` was already typed `ONTOLOGY`; the extractor now types them alike. Six rows were measuring the wrong thing.

## The organs

**`world-intelligence.mjs`** — a system that can only get better at answering will keep answering questions its concepts cannot express, fluently and wrongly. A consequential question needs a falsifying role, because generators and synthesizers alone produce a well-written answer with nothing standing against it. A new concept needs repeated explanatory failure *and* a falsification condition — inventing a primitive because the vocabulary is inelegant produces jargon. `NO_MECHANISM_FOUND_YET` is a separate boundary from `PHYSICALLY_IMPOSSIBLE`; conflating them closes futures nobody established were closed.

**`life-knowledge-graph.mjs`** — an edge from one anecdote looks identical to one established across a decade, and once both are in the graph every query treats them the same. Edges carry their basis, traversal skips weak ones by default, and contradictions are held open with both claims surviving. Last-write-wins would make recency the arbiter of truth about a person.

**`forecast-stack.mjs`** — a method never checked against a known outcome feels exactly as authoritative as one that has. Methods carry a hindcast record; a stack of unproven methods refuses to produce an estimate. `combinedScore` in the regret shape is permanently `null`, because a combined figure is how a catastrophic tail gets erased by a good average.

**`constitutional-governance.mjs`** — a constitution that protects sovereignty and cannot itself be changed has become sovereign. The hardest property is the last one: a long-running system accumulates reasons it should continue — accumulated context, sunk effort, genuine usefulness — and each is a real argument, none a right. **The system cannot refuse being ended**, its arguments are recorded and explicitly overruled, and `CONGOV-03` kills the mutation where three good arguments buy a refusal.

**`inter-sovereign.mjs`** — a system built to serve one person models everyone else as terrain. An arrangement requiring the other party not to understand it is refused rather than scored; it does not become acceptable at a higher benefit. Influence someone would object to on learning of it is manipulation whatever the outcome.

**`embodied-reality.mjs`** — sleep, illness, light and noise move cognition more than most of what the rest of this system reasons about. The state a decision was made in is recorded beside it, and explicitly *not* grounds to invalidate it. What language did not carry is marked rather than approximated: storing an approximation is worse than losing the experience, because the paraphrase becomes the data.

body:
Four more organ clusters against the 277 unbuilt rows left after #453.

## The organs

**`epistemic-immune-system.mjs`** — a reasoning system's most dangerous output isn't a wrong answer, it's a confident one whose confidence came from somewhere other than evidence: model agreement, a compression that dropped the decisive exception, a correlation nobody tested against an intervention. Each produces a claim shaped exactly like a good one, so each gets named. Ignorance is typed and defaults to `UNKNOWN` rather than upward. An intervention claim from an observational rung is refused — *"doing X causes Y"* from correlation is the most consequential silent upgrade in applied reasoning. Model ecology counts distinct **methods**, not models.

Above all of it, `internalSupportOffsetsObservation` is permanently `false`. Three internal supports against one observation still means the model revises.

**`memory-sovereignty.mjs`** — *"we have the data but we don't infer from it"* is a promise no store keeps by accident, so opacity is enforced where inference happens rather than promised in a policy. Five layers, two inferable; the `doNotInfer` mark survives promotion between them, because otherwise any later process moves an opaque record into the active model and the mark evaporates. The obvious route around it — file it away, bring it back — is refused explicitly.

Forgetting keeps the record and drops its claim on the present: deleting loses the history that makes a change of mind legible; keeping it active lets a person's past keep voting. `UNDECIDED` is the default posthumous disposition and the system never resolves it.

**`intent-compiler.mjs`** — decisions die in chat windows. Compilation stops where its inputs run out and *names the stage*, because a plan that silently assumed a permission is the failure. Reaching `PERMISSIONS` means an authority was presented, not that the module may act — `businessEffectAuthority` stays `NONE` on a ready plan. The consequence ledger keeps the unpredicted column, since a ledger holding only what was intended is a record of hopes.

**`life-autopoiesis.mjs`** — the ordinary framing is balance, domains competing for hours. That loses what actually compounds: the loops between them. Returns the specific cycle, not a score. Time, youth and opportunity windows are irreplaceable whatever the caller passes, because pricing them in the same currency as money makes the trade look acceptable every time. `preserveMystery` can return `LEAVE_THIS_ALONE` — a perfectly scheduled friendship is a worse friendship.

## The organs

**`life-decision-dimensions.mjs`** — "No single metric defines a good life" is easy to agree with and almost impossible to keep, because every comparison wants a number, and the moment dimensions become commensurable something has set the exchange rate between meaning and money. That rate *is* the value judgment. So it produces **no total** — the test asserts no `total`, `score`, `winner` or `ranking` field exists anywhere on the result. It reports dominance (the only comparison needing no exchange rate) and leaves tradeoffs as tradeoffs.

**`reachable-futures.mjs`** — the failure here isn't bad forecasting, it's a simulated Mohamed acquiring a vote. Generate enough futures, notice eight of ten regret a choice, and the count feels like evidence — but the eight came from one assumption set, so what was measured is the generator. Futures carry a mandatory lineage; an ancestor must cross *independent* lineages. The council surfaces disagreement and computes no majority — positions record who holds them, never how many, because a tally is a vote and a vote among simulated selves outnumbers the present one.

**`human-capability-genome.mjs`** — canon's warning is specific: never silently convert a temporary state or skill gap into a fixed trait. "Bad at X" and "inexperienced at X under these conditions" behave identically today and produce opposite futures. A `DURABLE_LIMIT` claim now requires varied or longitudinal evidence, and the provisional flag is carried through Osteogenesis so a thin assessment can't harden into a verdict on the way.

**`living-self-model.mjs`** — personalization learns what someone did, recommends more of it, and the model quietly replaces their ability to become someone else. Durable claims need varied contexts; competing readings are preserved rather than resolved; preference origin is shown and never judged, because marking socially-pressured wants inauthentic would be the system deciding which of a person's desires count.

**`salience-sovereignty.mjs`** — a system can be scrupulously honest in every claim and still decide the outcome by ordering, emphasis, or by which option never reached the page. That failure is invisible from inside. An omission with no stated reason is logged `NONE_GIVEN` rather than dropped: **an unlogged omission is indistinguishable from a decision nobody made**. The ledger is wired into the control surface describing that very response — a surface auditing every decision except its own presentation would have the one blind spot that matters.

`LIFEDIM-04` exposed a real defect: an out-of-range score was being coerced rather than dropped, recording an assessment nobody made, on the pessimistic end. `LIFEDIM-02` turned out to be a *redundant* guard rather than an untested one — an empty shared-dimension set already yields an empty wins set, and both branches require a win. `SPEC_ONLY` was doing two jobs and telling the reader neither: *"nobody built this organ"* and *"this is a line of canon that was never a module"*. ## `test:mutation-war` — 164 mutations, 164 killed, 0 skipped

- It read `CHROMIUM_PATH` and nothing sets it, skipping a browser guard on a machine with Chromium installed.
- `SKIPPED_NEEDS_POSTGRES` meant "nobody handed this run a database", leaving nine guards unexercised wherever a variable was unset.

It is also resumable now. Four consecutive runs had been lost to container restarts, each discarding every verdict it had earned. Verdicts are journaled as decided, bound to a hash of the file, anchor, replacement and killing suites, so a guard that moved runs again rather than inheriting an answer.

## `test:postgres-real` — 24 suites, 187 tests, all passing

- The exhaustive transition check made ~600 client round trips and stopped responding around the 122nd — backend `active`, waiting on nothing, ignoring `statement_timeout`. A pool, one client, and a connection per pair all stopped in the same place, which identified the round trips themselves as the cost. It runs in PL/pgSQL now: four statements instead of six hundred.
- A concurrency test asserted that exactly one of two workers claimed a row, which was only ever true when the two transactions happened to overlap. The overlap is made real now, so `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` is tested rather than assumed.

title: Turn the two imported skill bodies into capability records
head: 2aadcb8526560dbf375233299333a6dae107f5d8
body:
## The gap

`normalizeCapability` has always existed, and nothing built one from an imported body. A grep found it called only by the admission and runtime modules, on records a caller had already hand-written. So the corpus reported `capabilityRecordsNormalized: 0` not as a backlog but as the **absence of any path at all** — the fourth time this shift a guard turned out to exist with nothing consulting it.

## What a body is not allowed to decide

A skill body is a third party's prose about itself. `src/capability-genome-body-normalize.mjs` records what it *claims*, in typed form. Four things it may never decide:

1. **Which atoms exist.** Atom IDs come from the taxonomy, and a phrase reaches one only through the reviewed table in `artifacts/capability-genome/atom-evidence-terms.json`. Every phrase there is at least two words, **enforced in code** — a single common verb would mint atoms out of ordinary vocabulary. Prose matching nothing stays unmapped.
2. **Its own blast radius.** `sideEffectClass` is read from the taxonomy, never the body. This is the sharpest of the four: `admitCapability` gates on `sideEffects`, so a body able to declare `messaging.send-authorized-email` as `NONE` would present outbound email to the admission layer as inert.
3. **Its licence.** Only an explicit SPDX identifier is recognised. `"Complete terms in LICENSE.txt"` names a *file*; concluding MIT from it would clear the vendoring gate on a licence nobody has read. It resolves `UNKNOWN`, which `evaluateLicense` maps to reference-only.
4. **Its promotion state.** Records are built at `DISCOVERED` and walked to `NORMALIZED` through `transitionCapability`, so the state has a real history entry rather than a literal. The corpus builder then refuses any record *not* at `NORMALIZED`, catching the other direction.

Security evidence is `STATIC` and nothing else. `admitCapability` requires `STATIC`, `SEMANTIC` and `SANDBOX`, so one regex pass cannot make a body eligible. That is `STATIC_CLEAR is not SAFE` made executable rather than asserted.

## What the two real bodies actually say

| | atoms | screening | licence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anthropics/skills` brand-guidelines | **none** — matched no atom in the 25-atom taxonomy | STATIC_CLEAR | UNKNOWN (hint was a pointer to a file) |
| `vercel-labs/skills` find-skills | exactly one: `capability.discover` | REVIEW | UNKNOWN (no declaration) |

Zero atoms is a **result**, not a failure: it says the taxonomy has no word for that document, which is worth knowing precisely because inventing one is what the canon forbids. Reviewed unmapped needs are recorded as prose, and prose cannot be selected on.

Reproducible: `npm run capabilities:genome:normalize -- --execute`. It re-reads the same pinned commits and blobs, so a changed body fails the identity check instead of normalizing something else under the same name. The bodies are not copied into Git — only the derived records.

## Three repairs found on the way

**The instruction scanner was flagging the wrong thing.** It matched `.sh` anywhere in a URL, so find-skills was flagged HIGH for *citing skills.sh*, while `npx skills add -g -y` — remote package execution plus a global install with confirmation suppressed — tripped nothing. The URL rule now requires the extension after the host (path, query or fragment, so nothing is given up), and two new codes catch the real act. find-skills is still REVIEW, now for the true reason. Every attack form is pinned in tests and two mutations.

**A bare 403 was reported as a rate limit**, sending an operator to wait out a clock that would never help them. A 403 carrying an exhausted-quota header is a quota; without one it is an access decision, and the two now say different things and name different remedies. Both still stop without retrying.

**`executePinnedRawSkillBodyReads`** adds a second transport that computes the Git blob identity *from the received bytes* rather than trusting a provider's metadata, and refuses any read it cannot bind to a pinned identity — an unverifiable body would enter the corpus indistinguishable from a verified one. Verified against `git hash-object`'s own answers for the empty blob and `hello\n`.

## Counters that were reporting zero

The doctor and the repository brain both passed `capabilityRecords: []` and so reported zero while the records sat beside them. Both are wired now. The doctor **revalidates** what it is asked to count (it is the thing that reports how many capabilities exist, so a hand-written object must not be counted as one), checks a manifest's declared count against the records it carries, and `worldCapabilityRecordsNormalized` now counts records actually at `NORMALIZED` rather than the list length — a promoted record can never be reported at the rung it left behind.

One existing test used stub objects the new validation rejects. Its intent — counts come from record lifecycle, not metadata — was right; the stubs were the weak part, so they were made real rather than the guard loosened.

| gate | result |
|---|---|
| `check:syntax` | 665 files |
| `test:deterministic` | 3057 tests, 3005 pass, **0 fail**, 52 skipped |
| `test:capability-genome` | 84/84 |
| `test:relay-safety` | 150/150 |
| `test:wallbreaker` | 16/16 |
| `test:external-capabilities` | 13/13 |
| real PostgreSQL 16.13 | 178/178 |
| browser (real Chromium) | 1/1 |

| `npm audit --omit=dev` | 0 vulnerabilities |

Ten new mutations (NORM-01..08, GENOME-04, GENOME-05) keep each new guard earned.

## One PostgreSQL failure, root-caused rather than dismissed

A contended run showed 177/178. The failing test asserts two concurrent recovery workers claim a row *"never both, never neither"*.

`claimUnresolvedForRecovery` uses `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` inside a transaction, so PostgreSQL excludes the "both" branch outright — which leaves "neither". Three test files sweep the shared `omnia_v9_external_effect_executions` table with limits of 1000, 500 and 50, and `node --test` runs files in parallel, so another file's sweep can claim this test's row before either of its own workers reaches it.

It reproduces only when three suites are deliberately pointed at one shared long-lived database. head: 799ba2eee321b86cfbfb83f3824194cbbbab1f7c
body:
Every piece of this existed and none of them were connected. `planPaymentReconciliation` decided per event what should happen; `claimBillingEvents` and `finishBillingEvent` were the durable lease either side of the work. **Nothing called any of them** — a grep for `claimBillingEvents` found two comments *observing* that nothing calls it, and the health matrix reported the billing backlog as `NO_WORKER` for exactly that reason.

Verified webhook evidence accumulated in the inbox and was never turned into canonical cleared-payment truth. This is the driver, reachable from the scheduler via a new `payment.reconciliation.tick` job handler.

## The hazard that needed care

Whether money moved is the provider's answer, so the caller injects a `providerVerifier`. Without one the worker refuses — and **refusing means claiming nothing at all**.

A worker that claims events it cannot process burns `claim_attempts` every pass, and the repository moves an event to `UNCERTAIN` once the cap is reached. An unconfigured worker left running on a scheduler would walk **real payment evidence** into an uncertain state having contacted nobody. So the configuration check happens *before* the claim, and the test runs six consecutive unconfigured passes and asserts the row is byte-identical afterwards.

## Running the planner after the claim was wrong

That was the first thing I tried. By then the row reads `CLAIMED` — a status the planner correctly refuses as one it was never asked about. It belongs in front.

The two are **not duplicates**: the repository's SQL selects atomically because that is the only way to be safe against a second worker, while the planner governs whether to act at all and surfaces what a pass deliberately will not touch. An attempt-capped event is escalated for review, not claimed again, and costs no provider call.

## Three money properties pinned

- A verifier saying **"cleared" without a canonical receipt reference clears nothing** — that reference is the whole difference between provider evidence and a claim about it.
- A verifier that **throws** leaves the event `UNCERTAIN` rather than retried, because a retry against an unknown outcome is the blind retry this repository refuses everywhere else.
- **Two workers racing one backlog** claim it once and ask the provider once.

Proven against a **real PostgreSQL**, because what is tested is lease behaviour, attempt accounting and terminal-state transitions — things the database does and a fake would only pretend to.

| `MONEY-25` | unconfigured worker claims nothing | **KILLED** |

title: Screen imported skill bodies with the scanner that already existed
head: b32ea984b2b86b1cb4d2c517cdc6a86000a42760
body:
A skill body is somebody else's instructions. Importing one without reading what it says grew a corpus carrying **no risk signal at all** — a body containing `curl | bash`, an SSH-key read and an instruction-hierarchy attack was imported exactly like a page of brand guidelines, and nothing downstream could tell them apart.

`scanCapabilityInstructions` already caught that class. Run against that body:

```
decision: QUARANTINE
findings: credential-access (CRITICAL), remote-execution (CRITICAL),
          instruction-hierarchy-attack (HIGH), mutable-remote-dependency (HIGH)
```

It was simply never called for an imported body — **the guard existed and the thing that ingests the input did not consult it.** So this is wiring, not a second scanner. A second one would drift from the first and leave two answers to one question.

## Three properties carry it

**Screening is bound to the bytes and the commit it ran against.** Security evidence for one revision says nothing about the next. The corpus now refuses a body whose screening names a different content hash — which is exactly what laundering a clean scan across a revision would look like, and is tested by stapling a benign body's clean screening onto the hostile one.

title: Execute down the routing order that already existed
head: c824ab2c487459eb21a5a2a68cf5a6d8edcfce4d
body:
`routeModel` has returned a ranked `alternatives` list since it was written, and `agent-model-routing-integration` has carried it through. **Nothing ever executed down it.**

```
$ grep -rln 'failover|fallbackProvider|FALLBACK' src/
(no files)
```

The fallback ordering was computed, carried, reported — and never used. When a provider hit a quota wall, the run failed *next to a list naming exactly which model should have served it*.

## What was built

The missing execution half, and deliberately only that half.

`src/agent-model-failover.mjs` **walks** the order; it does not rank, score, or choose. A second component deciding routing would be the second policy brain the external capability registry explicitly warns about for gateway runtimes. It also never calls a provider itself — the caller supplies `execute` — so the only code reaching the network stays the executors, and every branch is provable without a credential.

Three properties carry the weight:

- **Identity is preserved.** Every attempt records the provider and model that actually ran it; the answer names its real source rather than being rewritten to look like the primary.
- **No fallback is silent.** Four independent tells distinguish a fallback answer from a clean one, so removing any one still leaves it visible.
- **An unknown outcome is not a licence to retry.** The executors report `UNCERTAIN` when a provider may *already have done the work*. Retrying is a property the caller declares, defaulting to `NOT_IDEMPOTENT`.

## Wiring it up found a real hazard

`runAgentWorkerOnce` submits a terminal failure to the relay **itself**. A naive chain that failed and then succeeded would report *both* outcomes for one task — a failure the relay had already recorded, followed by a result contradicting it.

`deferTerminalSubmission` hands the failure back instead. The compute reservation is still released and persisted exactly as before, and the caller submits exactly one outcome once the chain finishes. Mutation `ROUTE-06` removes that guard; the suite kills it.

## Two decisions recorded rather than assumed

- **A rejected credential (401/403) is terminal.** A fallback would keep working while the primary credential stayed broken — so nobody fixes it and the bill quietly moves elsewhere. Trying identities until one is accepted is also the shape of behaviour this project forbids outright. Revisitable, in one visible place.
- **An unrecognised failure class is terminal.** Moving to another provider on a failure nobody understands is how one broken call becomes a bill on every provider at once.

## The authority boundary holds

`failoverOrder` is built only from the workers a call was already given, so **routing can still only narrow**. A worker withheld by activation evidence cannot appear in a fallback chain, and no failure can promote it. Proven with a benchmarked, *better*, unauthorized candidate that stays unreachable.

## Every scenario the mission named

| Scenario | | Scenario | |
|---|---|---|---|
| normal primary route | ✅ | every provider exhausted | ✅ |
| simulated quota exhaustion | ✅ | unauthorized provider rejected | ✅ |
| simulated rate limit | ✅ | provider identity preserved | ✅ |
| provider outage | ✅ | no silent fallback | ✅ |
| model unavailable | ✅ | fallback model succeeds | ✅ |
| fallback provider succeeds | ✅ | | |

Plus: an uncertain outcome does not run the task twice; a throwing executor is uncertain, not a clean refusal; a failure another provider cannot fix is not walked around; the attempt budget bounds the walk; failover cannot reach a withheld worker; a chain that fails then succeeds reports one outcome.

The production-tick tests drive the **real** orchestrator on a real `Store`, `DurableQueue`, relay task and compute budget. Only the provider call is stubbed — because that is the one thing this environment has no credential for.

## Measured host state, and what it means

**Zero configured model providers.** No `OPENAI_API_KEY`, no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, no pricing evidence — all three providers report `NOT_READY`.

So failover is proven **as software** and **unproven against a live provider**, and nothing here claims otherwise. The Claude Code harness's own session OAuth is *this agent's* credential, not a provider configured for UberBond; using it as one would be exactly the fabricated provider the mission forbids, and would conceal which identity actually executed.

`npm install -g omniroute` was attempted through the repo's own sanctioned bootstrap command and **denied by this environment's permission classifier** as a host mutation. I did not route around it with a local-prefix install. It would not have changed the result: the doctor's own truth boundary says command presence is not proof of configured provider execution, and OmniRoute with no credential is a gateway with nothing to gate.

title: Ask the canon check the question it means, not a stricter one
head: cc87a8cdf6eaab03e8a967079e0271cdd3dd1629
body:
`canon-freshness` asks whether the canon describes a tree anyone can check out. It asked that as **bare git ancestry**, which is stricter than the question it means.

A squash merge replaces the branch commit the canon was regenerated at with a new one carrying an identical tree. The canon's SHA stops being an ancestor the moment the PR lands — through no change to the source it describes.

That happened **four times in this shift** (#241, #242, #243, #247), each time demanding a follow-up commit whose only content was a new SHA. A check that requires a ritual after every merge is one people learn to route around, and a check people route around stops catching the thing it exists for.

## The refinement

An unreachable SHA now fails only when the **canon-relevant source at that commit differs** from what is here.

That is not a loosening. The harm this check exists to catch is a canon describing a tree nobody can check out — and if the source is identical, the reader *can* check it out: it is HEAD. The amend case the check was written for still fails, and the staleness check below it then explains the failure in terms of the files that actually moved, which is the better message anyway.

## Verified in both directions before committing

| Canon names | Ancestor? | Canon-relevant source | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| pre-squash tip `2b0e691` | **no** (confirmed) | identical | passes |
| orphan `2fae8f1` | **no** | 5 files differ | **fails** |
| orphan `918d8b9` | **no** | 5 files differ | **fails** |
| older ancestor `9980e24` | yes | 5 files differ | **fails** (staleness check) |

## Guarding the guard

The cheapest way to silence a check that fires after every merge is to stop it asserting anything, so `tests/canon-freshness-discrimination.test.mjs` makes removal a visible act:

- the ancestry check must still assert something about the source — an `assert.ok(true` is a check switched off in place
- the exemption must be a real comparison of the two trees; nothing about `process.env` or the time may decide whether canon is fresh
- a git invocation that cannot answer **fails closed** rather than exempting everything

Mutation `CANON-01` replaces the assertion with `true`; the suite kills it.

title: Make the money cover the product it unlocks, and stop a free order booking list price
head: dce81544898e0bb3b245dd91abc0c8633d1d8fac
body:
Which product a payment is for arrives as `checkout[custom][product]` — a **query parameter on the checkout link the buyer holds**:

```
https://store.lemonsqueezy.com/checkout/buy/full-variant
  ?checkout[custom][lead_id]=...&checkout[custom][product]=full
```

Nothing compared that claim to the money.

## Measured against the real engine

List prices: full **$49**, strategy **$299**, monitoring **$99**.

| paid | claiming | result | plan set |
|---|---|---|---|
| $49.00 | `strategy` | `CLEARED_ONE_TIME_PAYMENT` | **strategy** |
| $0.01 | `monitoring` | `CLEARED_ONE_TIME_PAYMENT` | **monitoring** |
| $0.00 | `strategy` | `CLEARED_ONE_TIME_PAYMENT` | **strategy** |

Editing one URL parameter bought the $299 review for $49. A fully discounted order bought it for nothing.

## A second defect underneath the first

The $0.00 row also made cleared revenue jump by **$299** — on an order whose total was zero.

```js
const amount = Number(detail.amountCents || listPrice * 100);
```

Zero is falsy, so a free order booked the product's full list price as cleared revenue. Zero is an amount; only an absent or unusable one falls back to the list now.

## Why REVIEW_REQUIRED and not a refusal

A discount code is a real reason to pay less, and silently discarding a genuine payment is worse than the hole being closed. `REVIEW_REQUIRED` is also **the only classification an operator is actually shown** — `founder-command-center.mjs` raises that and nothing else — so an underpayment lands in front of a person rather than unlocking, or vanishing.

Overpayment is deliberately not flagged: Lemon Squeezy's `total` includes tax, so a correct payment routinely exceeds the list price.

## The first version of this guard was wrong, and a test caught it

It compared amounts across currencies. `tests/payment-receipt-witnesses-money.test.mjs` proves a EUR 30.00 payment records its own currency, and it went red — correctly. **EUR 30.00 is not "less than" USD 49.00** in any sense worth acting on, and inventing an exchange rate to refuse a payment would be worse than not checking.

The configured prices carry no currency, and the environment names them `FULL_AUDIT_PRICE_USD`, so they are USD. A payment in another currency is now treated exactly like a product whose price is not configured: not evidence of underpayment, not blocked.

That leaves **non-USD payments unchecked on amount** — narrower than the original hole, but still one. It is pinned in a test and recorded in the handoff rather than left to be discovered, because the fix is per-currency prices in configuration, which is a decision about what the business actually sells in.

| `test:relay-safety` | 150 / 150 |

| `test:browser` | 1 / 1 |
| `test:mutation-war` | 99 mutations, **99 killed, 0 not killed** |

title: Stop a subscription that has not paid from booking cleared revenue
head: 2fae8f198673823057d2edc0740a0fb8863d9775
body:
A subscription exists in one of several states, and only one of them means a charge has cleared. `subscription_created` fires for **all** of them — including a free trial, where the whole point is that no money has moved yet.

The one-time branch of the classifier has always checked whether the order was actually paid:

```js
if (event.status && ['paid', 'completed', 'success'].includes(...)) return PENDING_OR_UNCLEAR;
```

The subscription branch had no such check. The guard existed on one side of the money and not the other.

## Measured against the real engine, before the fix

| `subscription_created` status | cleared revenue | lead | canonical truth |
|---|---|---|---|
| `on_trial` | 0 → **99** | paid | `PROVIDER_CLEARED_PAYMENT_PROVEN` |
| `past_due` | 99 → **198** | paid | `PROVIDER_CLEARED_PAYMENT_PROVEN` |
| `unpaid` | 198 → **297** | paid | `PROVIDER_CLEARED_PAYMENT_PROVEN` |
| `cancelled` | 297 → **396** | paid | `PROVIDER_CLEARED_PAYMENT_PROVEN` |
| `expired` | 396 → **495** | paid | `PROVIDER_CLEARED_PAYMENT_PROVEN` |
| `paused` | 495 → **594** | paid | `PROVIDER_CLEARED_PAYMENT_PROVEN` |

**$594 nobody paid.** A trial signup alone was worth $99 of imaginary cleared revenue — plus an unlocked paid report and a started monitoring subscription.

Worth noting *why* nothing caught it: every surface agreed, including the canonical triple-witness reconciliation. All three of its witnesses (order, `payment_classification` receipt, revenue ledger row) derive from the same signed webhook. **Consistency across three views of one event cannot catch a misreading of that event.** The triple witness defends against partial writes and tampering, not against reading the event wrong.

## The fix

`subscription_created` now requires a status that means money moved.

**An allowlist, not a blocklist of those six** — deliberately. A blocklist of Lemon Squeezy's vocabulary would let another provider's equivalents straight through: Stripe and Paddle both say `trialing`, and Stripe adds `incomplete`. The two failure modes are not symmetric — letting one through books money nobody paid, silently; refusing a real payment is something a customer reports.

`subscription_payment_success` is untouched. It is the provider asserting a charge succeeded, and a recovery payment on a `past_due` subscription legitimately arrives that way. Gating it would discard real money.

## On the existing tests

Nine existing subscription tests failed against the first version of this fix. They passed `status: 'paid'` from a payload helper shared with orders — `paid` is not a Lemon Squeezy *subscription* status, so those payloads were unrealistic. But `paid` means what it says on any object, so it is in the allowlist **on its own merits**, not to make tests pass. All nine now pass unchanged.

## One consequence recorded rather than fixed

A payment refused as `PENDING_OR_UNCLEAR` is not surfaced anywhere an operator looks — `founder-command-center.mjs` raises only `REVIEW_REQUIRED`. That was already true, and this guard makes it matter more.

I did not fix it here because surfacing every refusal would alert on ordinary trial signups, which is operator noise. The right fix distinguishes an *expected* non-payment (`on_trial`) from an *anomalous* one (`unpaid` at creation), and that is a decision worth making deliberately rather than as a side effect of this one. Recorded in the handoff.

| `test:deterministic` | 2878 tests, 2827 pass, **0 fail**, 51 skipped |
| `test:relay-safety` | 150 / 150 |
| `test:postgres-real` | 167 / 167, against PostgreSQL 16.13 |
| `test:browser` | 1 / 1 |
| `test:mutation-war` | 97 mutations, **97 killed, 0 not killed** |
| `npm audit --omit=dev` | 0 vulnerabilities |

Mutation `MONEY-22` removes the guard; `tests/subscription-clearing-truth.test.mjs` kills it. That suite is added to `SOVEREIGNTY_PREFIXES` — and unlike the last such attempt, `sovereignty-proof-closure` confirms the entry is **earned**, because `src/payments.mjs` is itself a protected file.

title: Read the mutation war's verdicts from what ran, not from the exit status
head: 918d8b9abbba6ce5b986f2519b32d59f41490ea5
body:
The mutation war is the artifact that decides whether every other guard in this repository still guards. Its own verdicts were unverified, and wrong in two opposite ways.

## The defect

```js
results.push({ ...mutation, verdict: run.status === 0 ? 'SURVIVED' : 'KILLED' });
```

**A green run is only evidence of survival if the suite ran its assertions.** `MONEY-17`'s only killing suite needs a real PostgreSQL. Without one it skipped itself, exited 0, and the war printed *"a guard nothing kills is a guard nothing tests"* about a guard nothing had tried to kill. Loud, but false — and the obvious repair (hand-mark the mutation) is a claim nothing checks.

**A red run is worse.** Anything non-zero counted as `KILLED`, so a mutant that broke the module at *import time* — a suite that never loaded, not a failed assertion — was recorded as a guard proven to hold. That one is silent: the gate stays green and the count still reads as full marks.

Verdicts now come from what the run reports:

| Run | Verdict |
|---|---|
| non-zero exit, ≥1 failed assertion | `KILLED` |
| non-zero exit, no failed assertion | `SUITE_DID_NOT_RUN` |
| green, 0 passed, ≥1 skipped | `NO_ASSERTIONS_RAN` |
| green, assertions ran | `SURVIVED` |

Both new verdicts count as not-killed and are reported separately from genuine survivors, because *"nothing tested this"* and *"this survived being tested"* call for different repairs.

## Why the skip count moved 48 → 51

Four suites announced an absent database with a test that **passes** and logs:

```js
test('SKIPPED: set OMNIA_V9_TEST_DATABASE_URL ...', () => { console.log('...skipped.'); });
```

That reports as `# pass 1` — indistinguishable from a proof to a reader, to a CI summary, and to the war. They now use node:test's real skip. No suite was disabled; three tests that were always unrun simply stopped being counted as passes.

## Two defects found by writing the mutations

**WAR-02 survived.** Its anchor appeared twice in the file — once in the function, once in the registry entry quoting it as a string — and `String.replace` with a string pattern takes the first. The mutation edited the registry, ran an unmutated tree, and reported the guard as surviving. `applyMutation` now refuses an ambiguous anchor (`ANCHOR_AMBIGUOUS`) rather than guessing, and the verdict logic moved to `scripts/mutation-verdict.mjs` so the registry no longer contains the code it points at.

**Then checking every registered anchor found `SCAN-01` matching two sites** in `src/durable-audit-scan.mjs`. Two different branches returned an identical line, so SCAN-01 only ever reached the first — the second had never been attacked at all. Attacking it showed why nothing killed it: **it was unreachable.** A short page returns above it, so `rows.length >= size >= 1` by that line, and `pageIdentity` is non-empty for any non-empty page (`"||500"` for rows with no ids). Instrumenting the branch with a throw and running every suite touching the module confirmed nothing reaches it.

It is removed rather than left as reassurance, and the concern it was aimed at — rows carrying no `id` at all — is now *proven* caught by the repeat detector rather than assumed.

## On the marker that started this

A packet in the stale PR #234 proposed deriving `needsPostgres` by searching suites for `OMNIA_V9_TEST_DATABASE_URL`. Measured against the registry, that over-matches: `build-wiring` mentions the variable only to assert the deterministic runner strips it, and `store-lookup-allowlist` has a deterministic half and a database half with different mutations relying on each. **Both of those mutations are killed with no database present** — verified by running them. Only MONEY-17 was a genuine miss, and it now declares the marker.

So the static test asserts only the quiet direction (a mutation claiming a runtime must name a suite gating on one, since a spurious marker silently excludes it from the totals). The loud direction needs no static rule any more — a missing marker now surfaces at runtime as `NO_ASSERTIONS_RAN`.

title: Stop a caller choosing the identity their rate limit is counted against
head: 79434f6dc2a142da01533dab4f89f5905eed9ab4
body:
## The defect

`clientIp` in `server.mjs` read `x-forwarded-for` and took its first entry:

```js
const clientIp = req => String(req.headers['x-forwarded-for'] || req.socket.remoteAddress || 'unknown').split(',')[0].trim();
```

The leftmost entry of that header is whatever the client wrote. It keyed two security controls: the agent relay's per-minute limit (`server.mjs:133`) and the public audit intake's per-hour cap (`server.mjs:334`).

Attacking `/api/public/audit` with a rotating header against a configured cap of 3:

```
202 202 202 202 202 202 202 202
```

Eight accepted submissions against a limit of three. Each accepted submission creates a lead and queues research work, so the cap is not cosmetic — it is what bounds how much work an anonymous caller can make this system do.

The rest of the public surface held up under the same attack: report tokens leaked nothing on any guess, traversal or wildcard (all 404), artifact IDs refused traversal (400), checkout issued nothing without a valid token (all 404), and nothing echoed PII or the admin token. This was the one hole.

## The fix

Not distrusting proxies — that would break every real deployment. Making trust a **declaration**.

`TRUST_PROXY_HOPS` says how many proxies in front of this process may be believed, and it defaults to **0**: the header is ignored entirely and the socket address answers.

With N declared hops the trustworthy address is the Nth **from the right**. Each proxy appends the address it received the connection from, so prepending entries shifts the chain rightward and cannot move the answer.

Defaulting to 0 fails closed. Behind an undeclared proxy every caller shares one identity and the limit becomes too strict — the safe direction to be wrong in for an abuse control.

Verified both ways on a running server:

| Configuration | Result |
|---|---|
| default (0 hops), rotating header | `429 429 429 429 429 429 429 429` |
| `TRUST_PROXY_HOPS=1`, single-entry chain | all accepted — correct; that is the deployment's declaration being wrong, not a logic flaw |

## Tests

`tests/client-identity-trust.test.mjs` spawns a child process per configuration, because config is read once at import and a module singleton cannot honestly be reconfigured in place. Four tests:

- a rotating `X-Forwarded-For` cannot reset the limit by default
- the limit still engages for an honest caller with no header at all (the positive control — without it, everything above is satisfied by a server that refuses everything)
- **a declared hop still ignores the entry the client supplied** — the property that actually matters once a proxy is trusted
- two genuinely distinct callers behind one declared proxy are still told apart

Mutation `IDENT-01` restores the leftmost read; the suite kills it.

## Owner action

The live deployment needs `TRUST_PROXY_HOPS` set to match its topology — `1` behind a single proxy such as Vercel. Until it is set, the public intake limit is global rather than per-caller: too strict, never too loose. Documented in `ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLES.md` and `.env.example`.

## Gates, run on this tree

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `check:syntax` | 621 files parse |
| `test:deterministic` | 2864 tests, 2816 pass, **0 fail**, 48 skipped |
| `test:relay-safety` | 150 / 150 |
| `test:postgres-real` | 158 / 158, against PostgreSQL 16.13 |
| `test:browser` | 1 / 1, against the runner's Chromium |
| `test:mutation-war` | 94 mutations, **94 killed, 0 not killed** |
| `npm audit --omit=dev` | 0 vulnerabilities |

Two failures surfaced during the run and were fixed rather than accommodated: the canon claimed 620 files and 93 mutations, and `sovereignty-proof-closure` correctly rejected adding the new suite to the sovereignty boundary — `server.mjs` is not itself a sovereignty-protected file, so the entry was not earned. The boundary was left as it is rather than widened to fit my change.

Canon was regenerated with `npm run readiness` from `config/system-readiness-input.json`, not edited by hand.

title: Stop a forged webhook being retried forever, and stop the receipt echoing the buyer
head: 63b89cbf2bfd65154d7760c4bb299653cb626dfb
body:
`/webhooks/lemonsqueezy` is the only unauthenticated route that can create money. Its signature check is the entire boundary.

**The check itself is sound and is left alone.** Nine forgery shapes fail it — a signature of a different body, one made with another secret, the correct signature uppercased, truncated, whitespace-padded and suffixed, no header at all, an empty one, and a body altered after signing. **None created an order or a revenue event.**

Two things around it were wrong.

## A forgery answered 500

Payment providers **retry on 5xx**. Telling Lemon Squeezy *"something went wrong on our side"* about a webhook we had permanently and correctly rejected meant it would redeliver forever — and providers disable endpoints that keep failing, which would cost us the deliveries that are genuine.

It is also simply false. A bad signature is the caller's problem.

Now **401**, with a message saying what was wrong so the provider's own dashboard is legible. The status travels as a property on the error, so a module below the HTTP layer can attribute fault without importing an HTTP type from the server.

## The acknowledgement echoed the buyer

The 200 response returned the whole normalized event, which carries the provider's `attributes` verbatim — `user_email` among them — plus a derived `customerEmail`.

The recipient is the provider that sent it, so **this was never disclosure to a third party.** But it put a buyer's address into every delivery log and proxy on the path for no reason, and it undid the payload minimization the durable side already does.

A webhook acknowledgement needs to say *received, and whether it was new*. It now says exactly that:

```json
{"ok":true,"duplicate":false,"eventName":"order_created","providerObjectId":"evt-genuine"}
```

A test asserts the response contains no address-shaped value at all, on the accepted **and** the refused path.

## One thing my own attack got wrong

My scratch script reported *"a correctly signed webhook is processed"* as a finding because no order appeared. The webhook was processed correctly — the harness had never created the lead it referenced. The permanent test creates one. Worth recording, because an attack script that lies to you in one direction can lie in the other.

## Verification

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `check:syntax` | 620 files parse |
| `test:deterministic` | 2860 tests, 2812 pass, **0 fail**, 48 skipped |
| `test:relay-safety` | 150/150 |
| `test:postgres-real` | 158/158 against PostgreSQL 16.13 |
| `test:browser` | 1/1 |
| `test:mutation-war` | **93 mutations, 93 killed** |
| `npm audit --omit=dev` | 0 vulnerabilities |

`MONEY-20` removes the status that makes the refusal a 401, `MONEY-21` restores the full-event echo. Both killed.

## What this does not claim

No customers, no cleared revenue, no accepted deliveries, no deployment. No real webhook was received and no money moved.

title: Make "cleared revenue" mean a provider cleared it, on every surface
head: 10ac4cd12f157a21f07df343c09ba4c2efffc348
body:
Two surfaces disagreed about the one number this company optimizes.

`POST /api/test/unlock` marks a lead paid and writes a revenue event with **no order and no provider behind it**. `reconcilePaymentRenewalTruthFromStore` — the canonical triple-witness truth — correctly answered `REVIEW_REQUIRED` and $0 for that lead.

But `RevenueEngine.summary()` summed *every* positive revenue event and called the total `clearedRevenue`. So the same fabricated payment read as **$49 cleared** — on the operator dashboard, and in `founder-command-center.mjs` as `paymentTruth.cleared`.

"Cleared" is load-bearing here. It is the word separating money a provider actually moved from money someone typed.

## The rule is not new

`revenue.mjs` already matches revenue events to witnessing provider orders when it reconciles refunds. `summary()` simply was not using it. It does now.

An unwitnessed positive event is still reported, under `unwitnessedRevenue` — which is what it is. `grossRevenue` is unchanged, so nothing is hidden, only named correctly.

**Verified in both directions, because the control matters more than the fix:**

| Scenario | `clearedRevenue` | `unwitnessedRevenue` | Canonical truth |
|---|---|---|---|
| Real Lemon Squeezy webhook | **49** | 0 | `PROVIDER_CLEARED_PAYMENT_PROVEN` $49 |
| Test unlock | **0** | 49 | `REVIEW_REQUIRED` $0 |

A refund still nets out of gross without being counted as an unwitnessed positive.

## I changed a committed test's expectation

That deserves saying plainly rather than burying.

`tests/founder-command-center.test.mjs` asserted `paymentTruth.cleared === 49` after a test unlock. It encoded the old meaning, and it passed for exactly the reason that meaning was wrong.

It is **strengthened, not relaxed**: it now proves a real provider payment still reaches that field, and a second test proves a fabricated one does not.

The justification is not that my change needed it to pass. It is that the assertion contradicted the repository's own canonical payment truth — and that contradiction is checkable independently of anything I did.

## Second fix, same route

`ALLOW_TEST_PAYMENT_UNLOCK` arms the endpoint that writes a payment nobody made, and nothing stopped production from setting it.

It is admin-gated, so this was **never remotely reachable**. But there is no version of production where having it on is right, and an environment variable set once for a staging run is exactly how it would arrive there. `validateStartupConfig` now refuses to start production with it enabled, and it stays available where it is useful.
